findings.title: Percent parsing extracts an arbitrary unsigned substring
findings.body: The unanchored regex does not parse the complete numeric value and its result is dereferenced without checking. Consequently, `parseRate("-25%")` returns `0.25`, `.5%` returns `0.05`, and `1e2%` returns `0.01`; `%` throws a TypeError, while `abc25%` is silently accepted. This violates the requirement to return the represented fraction and creates both incorrect-rate and unexpected-exception paths.
findings.recommendation: Remove the `%`, validate or convert the complete remaining string while preserving supported numeric syntax and signs, and handle invalid or empty prefixes without dereferencing a null match.

next_steps: Correct the percent conversion and verify signed, fractional, exponent, malformed, and empty-prefix inputs.
